en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape.
The tamaraw, a small dwarf buffalo found only in Mindoro, is a critically endangered native mammal.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines and sits southeast of Metro Manila.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching 2,954 meters above sea level.
The waling-waling, called the queen of Philippine orchids, grows naturally in the tropical rainforests of Mindanao.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a protected marine sanctuary located in the middle of the Sulu Sea.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features an underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The amihan, or northeast monsoon, brings cool and dry air to the Philippines between November and February.
The Philippines is a major global producer of geothermal energy, harnessing volcanic heat from plants like Tiwi.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous farmers over 2,000 years ago.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, features a distinctive shaggy crest and hunts mainly in Mindanao forests.
